primitives.name: Presence Window Indicator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Live rooms open **only during windows when the founder or a deputized moderator is actually present**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W(t)': 'Boolean function indicating room presence at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Founder/moderator presence is deterministic and verifiable via escalation list.
primitives.breakdown_regime: W(t) = 0 when no authorized individual is present.

layer2.mapping: Binary temporal logic of room access mirrors binary state machines in GSE's event-driven architecture.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D(t)': 'Continuous-time distress signal strength at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Detection law is a threshold-based classifier with fixed sensitivity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: D(t) > θ implies immediate nudge activation.

layer2.mapping: Automated response kernel in GSE derived from static detection law in GSI's policy engine.

The presence window W(t) acts as a temporal gatekeeper, constraining the domain of possible actions in the community space. Distress signals D(t) operate as an external forcing function that can override normal operation only when integrated through the message pipeline. The moderation ladder L(n) represents a discrete control flow that maps violations to increasing penalties, forming a feedback loop against harmful behavior. Failure modes include false negatives in D(t), unauthorized access during absence of W(t), and cascading escalations due to misalignment in L(n). The system enforces a minimal viable policy through checklist compliance, ensuring that all components—presence, detection, and escalation—are synchronized before any live room opens.
